- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.4), model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently under-estimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); add 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude as a correction.
- Model over-estimates in early horizon (1–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.0x the 7-day average.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 2σ above recent 18-day mean, reduce by 10–20% of the deviation; if below, increase by 10–20%.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–2 days; if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0x the recent 7-day slope to forecast.
